EA APT UIX Format (.uix)

These are modular, compiled containers for EA's proprietary APT UI framework. They manage various layers of the UI stack, bridging engine data, physical inputs, and Adobe Flash/Scaleform assets.

Standard Chunk Structure

Regardless of their function, .uix files share a strict internal hierarchy:

  • uixf (Magic Header): The signature identifying the compiled UI container, followed by size and version allocations.
  • titl (Title Chunk): A null-terminated string declaring the internal module name (e.g., base, platform, TeamPhoto).
  • alig (Alignment Chunk): A structural block used to pad and align subsequent memory data.
  • apti (APT Payload): The core compiled data block, marked by the string Apt Data:74. This section houses 32-bit big-endian pointer tables, float arrays, and string pools.

Observed File Variants

Instead of a monolithic layout format, .uix files instantiate distinct object classes based on their role within the game's UI hierarchy:

  • Core Logic & Input Routers (base.uix, platform.uix): Act as the middleware between physical hardware and UI logic. They map specific controller inputs (PAD_LEFT, L1, JOYSTICK_RIGHT) to generic APT events (UI_EVENT_PAD_LEFT) and bind them to interactive ActionScript functions (ui_toggle_on_off, ui_slider).
  • Widget Layouts (TeamPhoto.uix): Small, discrete files defining specific visual elements. They encode raw typography calls (HighlanderStdBoldOut60), hex color arrays, and layout bounding boxes rather than active scripts.
  • Shared Dictionaries (SharedLibrary.uix): Act as centralized asset string pools containing universal textures (.tga files) and generic button templates loaded globally to prevent memory duplication.

Flash / Scaleform Integration

The hex data in base.uix explicitly confirms the APT framework relies on embedded Adobe Flash elements to drive the UI. Embedded strings reveal standard ActionScript paradigms:

  • MovieClip Execution: Engine handlers natively reference Flash objects and commands like movieClipAnimation, startMovieClipPulse, and standard layer targeting (_level0).
  • File Linkages: Layouts maintain hard references to paired Flash binaries (base.swf) and external scripting files (base.as, system.as).
  • Dynamic Property Hooks: The engine manipulates elements on the fly by targeting reserved instance names (placeHolder_mc) and built-in properties (_visible, setTextFormat, setRGB).
